messages.subject: eigendecomposition symmetric; instantiation model
parts:
I'll fix the eigenvalues to have two versions requiring
symmetry, symmetric inputs and self-adjoint inputs.
Both will use Eigen's self-adjoint solver, which mirrors
the lower triangular part of the matrix, but the symmetric
input one will test for symmetry to within a tolerance
(any suggestions? 1E-8 seems reasonable to me.)

I'm afraid the re-templatization of the matrix libs is
going to blow out some compilers. If so, we'll have to
go to an explicit instantiation model.

The basic code organization that makes most sense to me
is what Vandevoorde and Josuttis outline:

matrix.hpp // just the headers
matrix_def.hpp // complete header definitions
matrix_inst.cpp // explicit instantiations

To build header-only, include matrix_def.hpp.
To build with instantiation, include matrix.hpp and
link against compilation of matrix_inst.cpp.

The major-pain-in-the-ass downside is that you have
to list all of the template instantiations in matrix_inst.cpp.
This is easy for matrix for now with only double and
var. But when we mix in forward-mode auto-dif, the
combinatorics will be problematic.

- Bob
